# BioManager user guide

> BioManager is a free, open-source lab management app for a biology lab's animal colonies (mice, zebrafish, flies, worms and any other organism), plasmids, samples, orders, reagents, antibodies and viruses, with a calendar and a lab notebook. Website: https://biomanager.org. This file is the whole English user guide (https://biomanager.org/guide) in one place, followed by the guide to deploying a lab server; the Chinese guide is at https://biomanager.org/zh/guide.

---

## Using BioManager

Everything BioManager does, and how to move a lab into it: from a first launch to a whole lab on a shared server.

### Your first day

Six steps, in order. New here, or coming from spreadsheets? Read [Coming from Excel](https://biomanager.org/guide/coming-from-excel) first: it takes ten minutes and saves you days.

1. [**Install BioManager**: Download, unzip and open it. On a Mac, right-click → Open the first time. (2 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/install)

2. [**Set up your lab**: Create the first account, which is the admin, and tick what your lab keeps. (3 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/install#first-run)

3. [**Bring your lab in from Excel**: Import a sheet, and check the preview before anything is saved. (10 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/import-from-excel)

4. [**Work in a sheet**: Edit in place, fill down, sort and filter. (5 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/sheets)

5. [**Find anything**: Search everything with `⌘` `K`. (2 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/finding-things)

6. [**Invite your lab**: Approve sign-ups in Manage users, or give a visitor a guest pass. (5 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/invite-someone)

### Find your way

Or search the whole guide: press `/` or `⌘` `K`.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide

---

## What BioManager is

What BioManager keeps for a lab, and how it differs from a spreadsheet.

BioManager is one place for what a biology lab keeps: animals (mice, zebrafish, flies, worms, or any organism you describe), plasmids, samples, orders, reagents, antibodies and viruses, with a calendar and a notebook beside them. It looks and edits like a spreadsheet, but underneath it is a database that understands your lab: it knows a mouse lives in a cage on a rack, that a litter born today is weaned at P21, that a vial at 18 °C is flipped half as often as at 25 °C, and that an antibody expires next month.

It comes in two forms, the same program in both:

| Desktop app | For one person. macOS, Windows or Linux; your data stays on your computer. |
|---|---|
| Lab server | For a whole lab: one BioManager that everyone opens in a browser, the Android app, or from an iPhone's home screen. Usually free to host. [Every way to run one.](https://biomanager.org/server) The desktop app can set one up for you: **Settings → Set up a lab server** asks where it should go, does the work, and can bring your records along. |

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/what-it-is

---

## Coming from Excel

How your spreadsheets map onto BioManager, and what to do with each one.

If your lab runs on spreadsheets, you already know most of BioManager. The sheet is still there — click a cell and type — but each thing Excel makes you do by hand, BioManager does for you.

#### What you know, and what it becomes

| In Excel | In BioManager |
|---|---|
| A workbook with a tab per thing | Your lab, with a **database** per thing in the sidebar: Mouse, Fish, Plasmids, Orders… |
| A row | A **record** with a number that is never reused, so "mouse 1042" means one mouse forever. |
| Typing, then Save, then "who has the file open?" | Type in the cell; it **saves as you type**. Everyone edits the same records at once, and nobody's work overwrites anyone else's. |
| AutoFilter | The search box and the **chips** above every sheet: *All, Alive, Mine*, one per status. Your last choice is remembered, and it is in the page's address, so a bookmark or a link you send opens the sheet the same way. |
| Freeze panes, hide columns, column widths | The ID stays pinned as you scroll; **Columns** hides and shows; drag a column's edge to resize. Remembered per sheet. |
| Data validation drop-downs | **Choices** for a column (statuses, categories, purposes), set in **Configure** or **Dropdowns**. Renaming one renames it everywhere. |
| Autocomplete from the column | **Suggestions** from everything the lab typed before. In inventories, picking an earlier item fills in its vendor, catalogue number and price. |
| Fill down, copy a row | In the mice's **Add many** preview, click a cell and **Fill down** (or `Ctrl`/`⌘` + `D`) copies it to the rows below. **Duplicate** copies any record. |
| Paste a column | Copy a column of readings (a Nanodrop export, say) or a block of cells, click the first cell in the sheet and paste: the values go down the rows as shown, and across if you copied several columns, each saved as if typed. A number steps over a choice column it isn't one of (the unit between concentration and A260/280), and a note says which rows it went into, first to last, so a list in another order shows at once. |
| Formulas for age, wean and flip dates | Worked out for you: ages, P21 weaning, genotyping dates, flip schedules that follow the incubator's temperature. |
| Conditional formatting | Status pills, a dot for what is alive or in use (coloured by age for animals), expired stock in red — and the **Home** page gathering everything that needs you today. |
| VLOOKUP between sheets | Real links: a mouse is in a cage on a rack; a sample came from that mouse; an order became that reagent. Click through. |
| Version history, "who changed this?" | The **Audit log** records every edit, who made it and what it was before; **Batch history** undoes any bulk change. |
| Mail-merge for cage labels | **Cage cards** sized for card stock, each with a QR code that opens the cage on a phone. |
| Your old workbook | **Import from Excel** on every database reads it as it is, whatever its columns are called. |
| Save As CSV | **Export** on every sheet (CSV; for mice also Excel and PDF). Your data is never locked in. |

Once BioManager is installed and the lab is set up, [bring your sheets in](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in): about half an hour.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/coming-from-excel

---

## Install and set up

Install the desktop app, open it the first time, and set up your lab.

#### Get it

| macOS | [Download](https://biomanager.org/download), unzip, drag **BioManager** into Applications. The first time, **right-click it → Open**, then Open. |
|---|---|
| Windows | Extract the zip, open the **BioManager** folder, run **BioManager.exe**. At the warning choose **More info → Run anyway**. Its window uses Microsoft Edge WebView2, which Windows 11 has; on a Windows 10 PC without it, BioManager offers to download it from Microsoft and opens in your web browser meanwhile. Install it, then open BioManager again for its own window. |
| Linux | Mark `BioManager-Linux.AppImage` executable (right-click → Properties, or `chmod +x`) and open it. |
| Updates | The desktop app checks for a new version once a day and offers it, with what's new; **BioManager → Check for Updates…** (on Windows and Linux, **Help**) asks now. **Install and Restart** downloads it, checks it, and swaps it in as the app quits; where it can't (the Linux `.tar.gz`, a folder it can't write to), it opens the download to install as above. Your data stays where it is, and before a new version changes it a copy is kept ([Your data](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data)). Turn the daily check off with **Check for Updates Automatically**. |
| What's new | After an update, on a desktop or a lab server, the first page you open shows a short **What's new**: what is new, what works differently and what was fixed, with a link to the full notes. **Got it** closes it for good; **Help → What's new** opens it again. |
| A lab server | Nothing to install: open the address your admin gives you. A welcome page shows what BioManager does and leads to **Sign in** or **Create an account**. Setting one up is on [Run it for your lab](https://biomanager.org/server). |
| Phones | The Android app, or your lab server added to an iPhone's home screen: see [Phones and cage cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/phones-and-cage-cards). |

> **Why the warning on a computer?** The apps aren't signed by Apple or Microsoft, so the system asks you to confirm once per version.

#### The set-up survey

The first account is the lab's **admin** (on a server, it needs the one-time setup code printed when the server started). The admin then answers a short survey, and BioManager builds exactly what you'll use — nothing more:

1. **Your lab** — its name, time zone, how dates are written and the genotyping day ([what these do](https://biomanager.org/guide/lab-setup)).

2. **What does your lab keep?** Tick animals and stocks (mice, zebrafish, flies, worms, other organisms) and molecular and supplies (plasmids, samples, orders, reagents, antibodies, viruses). For each, a little more: a name (e.g. *Mouse room B*); for the colony how many racks, their size and how positions are labelled; for flies and worms which incubator temperatures you run. Blank means the usual.

3. **Which lab functions?** The calendar and the notebook.

4. **What may members do?** Whether members may create databases of their own, whether they may add databases for the whole lab, whether they may keep a copy of the lab on their computers, and whether they may make [API tokens](https://biomanager.org/guide/scripts-and-api).

Below the questions, **Send BioManager's makers anonymous counts once a day** is ticked; untick it if you'd rather not ([what is sent](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data#counts)).

BioManager then makes those databases, the racks and incubators too, and takes you Home. Everyone who joins later gets a one-page welcome tour of the lab's databases on first sign-in (**Settings → See the welcome tour again** brings it back).

**English or 中文.** BioManager shows in the language your computer or browser asks for first, English or Simplified Chinese. Choose for yourself under **Settings → Language**, or with the **中文 / English** switch on the sign-in page. Everyone in the lab chooses their own; names, notes and everything people type stay as written.

### Troubleshooting

#### The app won't open on my Mac

Right-click it and choose **Open**. If macOS says it's damaged, move it to Applications first, then try again.

#### Linux: the AppImage does nothing

Mark it executable. If it still won't start, install `libfuse2`, or use the `.tar.gz` and run `BioManager/BioManager`.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/install

---

## Bring your lab in

Move your records in: import sheets, add many at once, and check what came in.

About half an hour, once the lab is set up. There are two ways in: **Import from Excel** for the sheets you already keep, and **Add many** for a new group you describe once.

1. **Make your racks first.** **Cages → Rack grid → New rack**, named as in your sheet and labelled like the stickers on the real racks. Then a sheet with *Rack* and *Position* columns puts every cage in its place; anything without a position waits in *Unplaced* for you to drag on (on a tablet: **Move**, tap the cage, tap its place).

2. **Open Import from Excel.** Every database has it in the toolbar above its sheet — Mice, Fish, Plasmids, fly and worm vials, any organism and every inventory. **Choose a file** (`.xlsx`, CSV or TSV, up to 15 MB and 5,000 rows) and press **Continue**. If the workbook has several sheets, pick one above the matches. No template, no renaming columns.

3. **Check how the columns were matched.** BioManager matches by meaning, not just by name: *Position*, *Slot* and *Well* are the position, *DOB* and *Born* the date of birth, *Supplier* the vendor, *Cat. No.* the catalogue number. Where a name could mean two things the values decide — a *Location* of `A1`, `B2`… is a position in a box, one of `Freezer 2` is a location. Each match says why; change any of them.

4. **Nothing is lost unless you say so.** A column BioManager doesn't have becomes a new column in an inventory or organism database (if you may configure it), or goes **Into the notes** as `Header: value`; choose **Leave out** to skip it. A must-have column your sheet lacks, like the owner, gets one value for every row — for plasmids and stock, also whether every row is *Personal* or *Lab common* (a *Lab common* column says it row by row). Dates stay as Excel wrote them (`3/14/2026`, `14/03/2026`, `12-May-26`): each column decides whether day or month comes first, and when it can't tell, Lab setup's date style does. A date that can't be read, or a birth date in the future, is left blank and kept in the notes. *Male*, *m* and *♂* all become M; statuses and people are matched by name. A *Cage #* typed once and merged down over its mice counts for each of them, and the cages the import makes belong to their mice's owner.

5. **Preview, then import.** **Preview the import** runs every row through the same checks as the database's own form and lists any that would be skipped, by its row number in Excel. A *Total* line under the records is left out, and a mouse whose ID is already taken (in the colony, or by an earlier row) gets the next free one, with yours kept in its notes; the preview says so for each. **Import 120 mice** (the button counts them) saves the rest as one batch, which **Batch history** can undo; **Change the matches** goes back a step.

6. **A new group, not a sheet?** For mice, **Add many** describes one mouse and how many, or loads the CSV from its **Download a template**. In any inventory and in Plasmids, **Add many** takes a list pasted straight from Excel — one name per line becomes one record each.

7. **Print cage cards** and put them on the cages. From now on, the spreadsheet is the backup, not the record.

### Troubleshooting

#### Rows were skipped on import

The preview lists each one by its row number in Excel and says why. Fix those rows and import just them: importing the whole sheet again would add the other rows a second time.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in

---

## Home

The page that opens each morning: what needs doing today, in three layouts.

Home is where each day starts: only what needs attention, from every database you can see. Choose how it looks with the **Layout** chips at the top (or in **Settings → Home layout**); the choice is yours alone.

- **Classic**: Cards: your databases as tiles, a few numbers (total mice, mice over 30 weeks, weanings, pending orders, notebook pages) and cards for *Mice older than 30 weeks*, *Upcoming weanings*, the *Genotyping queue*, *Flies & worms: due*, *Animal databases: due*, *Expiring & low stock*, zebrafish mating tanks to return, the *Next 14 days* and *Recent orders*.

- **Tracks**: Every dated job on one ruler of days, one track per kind of work, coloured overdue, today, within 3 days or scheduled. Choose 1, 2 or 4 weeks. *Needs you now* and *Busy days* sit beside it. On a phone it becomes a list of days.

- **Freezer**: Your racks seen from above, lit where something is due, with a **Pull list** of the next three days' jobs in walking order, to take into the room. A cage's cap colour shows its owner.

**Customize**, beside the layout chips, arranges Classic your way: tick the cards you want, drag them (or use the arrows; the double arrow sends a card to the top) into your order, and make any of them *wide*. Four cards start switched off and are there to add: *Your to-dos* (due this week or undated), *Bookings* (instruments booked in the next week), *Recent pages* of your notebook, and *Calculators* (the ones you opened last, then the usual ones). **Back to the usual** puts everything back, after asking. Like the layout, it is yours alone.

On every layout:

- **For you**: Your unread notifications.

- **Getting started**: While you're new, your first steps, each ticked off when it's done. An admin's list sets the lab up — add a rack, bring in your mice, print cage cards, set up your fly database, invite the lab. A member's is their own — find your mice, scan a cage card, request an order, add a plasmid, read this guide. **Hide this list** puts it away.

- **Upcoming weanings**: The same list the calendar shows; each row opens its cage.

*The Home page*

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page

---

## Working in a sheet

Edit records the way you edit a spreadsheet: click, type, and it saves.

- **Edit in place**: Click a cell and type, or pick from its list. It saves as you go; a note at the bottom says *All changes saved*. If a change can't be saved (say, a required field emptied) the cell turns red and says why.

- **The dot**: The dot beside the number means alive or usable: a living mouse, a vial in use, an open order, a reagent in stock; grey means it isn't. For animals its colour is their age: **blue** young, **green** adult, **red** old (mice: under 8 weeks, 8 to 30, past 30; fish: under 3 months, to 18 months, past 18; a vial or plate: progeny still developing, adults, past its flip or chunk). An expired reagent, antibody or virus is red too. Point at a dot to see what it means.

- **Scrolling and New**: The page scrolls, not the sheet: its search and buttons stay at the top of the window, its column names under them, and its count at the bottom. **All** under *per page* lists every row. **New**, at the bottom left, adds an empty row at the end of the sheet with its first cell ready to type in. A strain, fish, line, plasmid or order needs a name or a tank first, so there it opens the form.

- **Open a record**: The pencil opens the full record in a dialog, with every field, grouped. New records open the same dialog.

- **Sort, Columns, Export, Print**: **Sort** by any column, or click a heading. **Columns** hides what you don't need; drag an edge to resize. **Export** downloads the rows you see as CSV (mice: also Excel and PDF). **Print** gives a clean sheet. Your sort, filters, hidden columns and widths are remembered on that computer.

- **On a phone**: A sheet becomes one card per row: the number and its buttons on top, then each column by name. **Columns** still hides what you don't need there.

- **If a save is refused**: Say a tank ID is taken: the page tells you why and reopens the form with what you typed, so you fix one field, not all of them.

- **Layouts**: The layouts sit above the sheet, on the left, the same in every database. Where it fits, a sheet also shows as a **Rack grid** or **Box grid**: each tile shows its record's name and position; drag a tile to move it. On a touch screen, press **Move**, tap a tile, then tap where it goes — another tile swaps with it, *Unplaced* takes it out. Orders also show as a **Board**, a column per status: drag a card along.

- **Suggestions**: Text columns suggest what's been typed before, so the lab spells a vendor or a unit one way.

- **What ended long ago**: Mice that died, cages emptied, tubes used up and vials discarded over 90 days ago aren't listed, so a colony with years of history opens quickly. A line at the top says how many; **Show them** lists everything. Search still finds them, and the mouse export includes them.

### Troubleshooting

#### A cell turned red

That change wasn't saved; the message at the bottom says why (a required field, a date that isn't one).

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/sheets

---

## Many at once

Select many records and change, move or print them in one go.

- **Add many**: For a new group: describe one record and say how many. In inventories and plasmids you can instead paste a list of names, one per line. For mice, say how many females and males, or load a CSV (**Download a template** gives the columns); you then see an editable preview with the numbers that will be assigned. There, **Fill down** copies the cell you're in to every row below (`Ctrl`/`⌘` + `D` too), and nothing is saved until you press **Create**.

- **Import from Excel**: For the sheet you already keep. Every database takes an Excel workbook or CSV, with any columns: you check how they were matched, see a preview of what would be created and which rows would be skipped, then import them as one batch you can undo. See [Bring your lab in](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in).

- **Select and act**: Tick rows (shift-click selects a range) and a bar rises from the bottom: set a field, move, change owner or status, sac, retire, delete. **Set field** sets any column on them, your own columns included (a date column takes a date, a number column a number). That includes **Source**, where you pick the colony and type the ID once — handy when one mouse gives a dozen samples and each would otherwise be opened in turn. Records you may not change are skipped and counted, never silently changed.

- **Duplicate**: Copies a record as a new one of yours — the next aliquot, or the same order again.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/many-at-once

---

## Finding things

Search everything from anywhere, and keep pages open as tabs.

- **The search box** above a sheet filters it as you type: an ID, a genotype, a cage, a note.

- **Chips** beside it narrow it: *All*, *Alive*, *Mine*, *Lab common*, a status, *Expiring soon*.

- **Search everything** with `⌘`/`Ctrl` + `K`, from anywhere: mice, cages, litters, experiments, strains, vials, tanks, lines, clutches, plasmids, orders, samples, reagents, antibodies, viruses and notebook pages. Names that are, or start with, what you typed come first ("S20" finds the S20 tubes before a note about an S200 column), and a lot or catalogue number typed in full comes before anything that merely contains it. Arrows to move, Enter to open.

- **Tabs.** Following a link moves the tab you're in; **+** opens a new tab on your start page (**Settings → Default landing page**; Home if none). Drag to reorder, `Alt` (`⌥ Option` on a Mac) + `1`…`9` to jump. They're still there tomorrow, and they are yours: someone else signing in on the same computer gets their own.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/finding-things

---

## Undo and history

Undo a whole batch of changes from Batch history, and see in the Audit log who changed what, and when.

**More → Batch history** at the foot of the sidebar opens it: every bulk change — an Add many, a move, a status change on fifty rows, an import — with **Undo**. If someone has edited those records since, BioManager says so and offers **Undo anyway** rather than silently overwriting their work. Everyone sees their own batches; admins see the lab's. Changes an AI assistant proposed and you approved are here too, as one batch each ([AI assistants](https://biomanager.org/guide/ai-assistants)).

The **Audit log** (admins) records every create, edit and delete: when, who, which record, and exactly what changed — `genotype: DBH-Cre → ∅`.

### Troubleshooting

#### I made a mistake with a bulk change

**More → Batch history** in the sidebar → **Undo**.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/undo-and-history

---

## Notifications

The bell and what it tells you: your animals moved, orders arriving, @mentions and genotyping reminders, and how to choose them.

The bell at the top shows what happened while you were away: someone moved your animals or vials, picked from your breeders, recorded a genotype on your mice, an order you placed was ordered, arrived or was cancelled, someone wrote `@you` in a record's notes (a reagent, an order, a plasmid, a cage) or a notebook comment, and lab news such as being made admin. Admins are told of each new order request. A notice about one record opens that record — an order notice opens the order. A daily note reminds you of pups waiting to be genotyped. Choose which kinds you get in **Settings → Notifications**; you're never notified of your own changes.

If your server sends email, a daily digest of what's overdue or coming up — flips, weanings, returns, expiring stock — goes to the email on your profile (**Settings → Reminder emails**). Clear the email to stop it.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/notifications

---

## Keyboard shortcuts

Every keyboard shortcut on one page: search with ⌘/Ctrl K, switch tabs, fill down, and the Mac menu bar's keys.

| `⌘`/`Ctrl` `K` | Search everything |
|---|---|
| `Alt` `1`…`9` | Go to tab 1–9. On a Mac, `Alt` is `⌥ Option`, here and below. |
| `Alt` `←` `→` | Previous / next tab (also `Alt` `[` `]`) |
| `Alt` `W` | Close this tab |
| `⌘`/`Ctrl` `B` | Hide or show the sidebar |
| `Esc` | Close a menu or dialog |
| Shift-click | Select a range of rows |
| `⌘`/`Ctrl` `D` | Fill down, in the mice's **Add many** preview |

In the desktop app on a Mac, the menu bar has the usual ones as well:

| `⌘` `T` · `⌘` `W` | New tab · close this tab |
|---|---|
| `⇧` `⌘` `]` `[` | Next / previous tab |
| `⌘` `1`…`9` | Your databases, in the sidebar's order (all of the sidebar is in **Go**) |
| `⌘` `[` `]` · `⇧` `⌘` `H` | Back / forward · Home |
| `⌘` `,` | Settings |
| `⇧` `⌘` `E` · `⌘` `P` | Export this sheet · print |
| `⌘` `R` · `⌘` `=` `-` `0` | Reload · zoom in, out, actual size. **View → Appearance** sets light or dark whatever the system uses. |

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/keyboard-shortcuts

---

## Record a litter

When pups are born in a breeding cage, record the date once and BioManager works out when they are weaned and genotyped.

Who and where: Anyone who may edit the cage · Desktop and lab server

1. In the mouse colony, open the **Cages** tab. Not there? The **My colony / My groups / Shared / Everyone** switch changes which cages you see.

2. Find the breeding cage and open it with the arrow at the start of its row or its mice count, or find its card under **Cards**. **Litter born**, **Genotyping** and **Wean** are on cages whose purpose is *Breeder* or *Breeding*.

3. Press **Litter born**.

4. Check the **Date of birth**: it is today unless you change it, and a date in the future is refused. If the cage already has a litter date, the dialog says the new one replaces it.

5. Press **Record the litter**.

BioManager works out weaning (P21) and genotyping (P28, or the day chosen in [Lab setup](https://biomanager.org/guide/lab-setup)), which appear on Home and the calendar when due — the same list in both. In the cage's row, *Litter born* and *Wean due* come right after the mice. To make a record for each pup, go on to [Genotype a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter).

> **One litter date per cage** A cage holds one litter date, so a new litter replaces the last. If those pups are still in the cage, wean them first.

Related: [Genotype a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter) [Wean a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter) [Mouse colony](https://biomanager.org/guide/mouse-colony)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter

---

## Genotype a litter

Make a mouse for each pup of a new litter, then enter their genotypes when the results come back.

Who and where: Anyone who may edit the cage · Desktop and lab server

1. Once the litter is [recorded](https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter), open the breeding cage on the **Cages** tab and press **Genotyping**.

2. Check the **Father** and **Mother**, and type the number of **Pups**. Father and mother start as the cage's first male and female. Pups is a whole number from 1 to 40.

3. Press **Create litter**. BioManager makes the litter, numbered L-1, L-2, L-3…, and a mouse for each pup, set to *geno*. The pups are in that cage, and they are yours.

4. When the results are in, find the pups: **In the mouse sheet**, on the open cage, lists that cage's mice. On Home, the **Genotyping queue** lists mice waiting, and **View mice** opens the mouse sheet. The genotyping day (P28, or the one chosen in Lab setup) is on Home and the calendar, and a daily note reminds you of pups waiting to be genotyped.

5. Type each pup's result in its **Genotype** cell, and its sex if it isn't set yet. Each cell saves as you type.

6. Change each pup's **Status** from *geno* to what it is for now, such as *breeder* or *experiment*. For many at once, tick them and use **Set field**.

A pup waits in the genotyping queue on Home while its status is *geno*, and leaves it once that changes. If someone else records the genotype of your mice, you are notified.

Related: [Record a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter) [Wean a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter) [Home](https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page) [Many at once](https://biomanager.org/guide/many-at-once)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter

---

## Wean a litter

At P21, move the pups out of the breeding cage into cages of their own, and the litter leaves Home and the calendar.

Who and where: Anyone who may edit the cage · Desktop and lab server

1. Find the cage: on Home, each row of **Upcoming weanings** opens its cage; or open it on the **Cages** tab, where *Wean due* shows in its row.

2. Press **Wean**. Pups younger than P18 are weaned only after you confirm, with **Wean early**.

3. Check the rows in *Wean and distribute pups*. They start with the cage's pups, females and males on separate rows; the mice in a row go to one place. **Add row** adds another destination. The sex on a row is given to its mice. Mice not listed in any row stay in the cage.

4. For each row, type an **Existing cage**, or leave it empty for a new cage of yours, with **Card (new cage)** as its card's label. A filled *Existing cage* wins over *Card*.

5. Press **Wean and move**. To move the pups yourself later, press **Mark weaned, move pups later** instead.

Either way the litter is marked weaned and leaves Home and the calendar. Then [print cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/print-cage-cards) for the new cages.

### Troubleshooting

#### I weaned the wrong cage

A weaning is one bulk change: **More → Batch history** in the sidebar → **Undo**.

Related: [Record a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter) [Genotype a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter) [Print cage cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/print-cage-cards) [Mouse colony](https://biomanager.org/guide/mouse-colony)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter

---

## Print cage cards

Print a card for each cage, with a QR code that opens the cage on a phone at the rack.

Who and where: Anyone in the lab · Scanning needs a lab server

1. In the mouse colony, open the **Cages** tab and choose **My colony**, **My groups**, **Shared** or **Everyone**: the cards are for the cages you see. For one cage, the print button on its row or card prints just its card.

2. Press **Cage cards** in the toolbar. For tanks, vials and tubes: **Tank labels** (Zebrafish), **Labels** on a fly or worm database, and **Labels** on ticked samples, reagents or any inventory's rows.

3. Under **Print on**, choose a sheet of cards for any printer, or a label printer's roll: Brother QL (62 × 29, 90 × 29, 100 × 62 mm) or Zebra (2 × 1, 3 × 1, 4 × 2, 4 × 2.5 in). Press **Show**. Your choice is remembered. On a label printer it prints one label a page, typed to fit.

4. Press **Print**. For a label printer, pick it and that label size in the print dialog, with margins **None**.

5. For a Zebra, you can instead press **Download for Zebra (.zpl)**, or **Send to Zebra** once an admin has added its address on the lab's network (under **Send labels straight to a Zebra on the network**).

6. Put each card on its cage.

Each card shows the owner, purpose, where the cage goes (rack and position), its animals with how many of each sex, the genotype and a QR code. Scanning it opens that cage, ready to edit, at the rack.

> **Scanning on a phone** Phones reach a lab server, or a desktop that shares its lab on the network ([Devices](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data#devices)): otherwise the app on one computer is private to that computer.

### Troubleshooting

#### My phone can't reach the server

Check the address with your admin; that you're on the lab's network, VPN or Tailscale; and, if your lab uses its own certificate, that it's installed on the phone.

Related: [Phones and cage cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/phones-and-cage-cards) [Wean a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter) [Mouse colony](https://biomanager.org/guide/mouse-colony)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/print-cage-cards

---

## Import from Excel

Bring in the sheet your lab already keeps, as it is, with no template and no renaming of columns.

Who and where: Anyone who adds records · Every database

1. For mice, make your racks first: **Cages → Rack grid → New rack**, named as in your sheet. A sheet with *Rack* and *Position* columns then puts every cage in its place; anything without a position waits in *Unplaced*.

2. Open the database and press **Import from Excel** in the toolbar above its sheet (for mice, on the **Mice** tab).

3. **Choose a file** (`.xlsx`, CSV or TSV, up to 15 MB and 5,000 rows) and press **Continue**. If the workbook has several sheets, pick one above the matches.

4. Check where each column goes. Each match says why; change any of them. A column BioManager doesn't have becomes a new column in an inventory or organism database (if you may configure it), or goes **Into the notes**; **Leave out** skips it.

5. Give a value for any must-have column your sheet lacks, like the owner: it goes on every row. For plasmids and stock, also whether every row is *Personal* or *Lab common*.

6. Press **Preview the import**. It runs every row through the database's own checks and lists any that would be skipped, by its row number in Excel. **Change the matches** goes back a step.

7. Press the import button, which counts the records (**Import 120 mice**, say).

The rows are saved as one batch, which **More → Batch history** can undo. Dates stay as Excel wrote them, and one that can't be read, or a birth date in the future, is left blank and kept in the notes. A mouse whose ID is already taken gets the next free one, with yours kept in its notes.

### Troubleshooting

#### Rows were skipped on import

The preview lists each one by its row number in Excel and says why. Fix those rows and import just them: importing the whole sheet again would add the other rows a second time.

Related: [Bring your lab in](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in) [Coming from Excel](https://biomanager.org/guide/coming-from-excel) [Undo and history](https://biomanager.org/guide/undo-and-history)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/import-from-excel

---

## Receive an order into stock

When an order arrives, mark it received and add it to stock, with its details already filled in.

Who and where: Anyone who may edit the order · Desktop and lab server

1. Open Orders and find the order. The status chips, *Requested, Ordered, Received, Cancelled*, narrow the sheet to one stage.

2. Mark it received: set its **Status** to *received*, or on the **Board**, drag its card to the *Received* column.

3. BioManager asks **Add it to stock?** Under **Add to**, choose the reagents, antibodies or viruses it goes into, and under **Belongs to**, whether it is lab common or yours. **Not now** leaves it; later, the **To stock** button on the order does the same.

4. Press **Add to stock**.

5. The new record opens with its name, vendor, catalogue number, lot, quantity and expiry already filled in from the order. Add where it is kept. If that database needs a field the order doesn't have, its form opens filled in from the order instead: fill in the rest and save.

From then on the order shows *Reagents #8* and the reagent shows the order it came from; each opens the other. The person who requested the order is notified as it moves. When it runs low, **Order again** (the cart button on the reagent, antibody or virus) opens a new order with its details.

Related: [Samples, orders, reagents, antibodies, viruses](https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders) [Notifications](https://biomanager.org/guide/notifications)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/receive-an-order

---

## Book equipment

Book time on a shared instrument in the calendar, so two people never turn up for the confocal at once.

Who and where: Anyone in the lab · Desktop and lab server

1. Open the Calendar. If the instrument isn't listed under **Equipment** in its sidebar, press **Manage** there, give its **Name** and **Where**, and press **Add instrument**. **Edit** one there to rename it, say where it is or change its colour; its bookings follow.

2. Press the arrow beside **New event** and choose **Book equipment**. Or press **New event** and choose **Booking**.

3. Pick the **Instrument**, the **From** and **To** times, and say **What for**.

4. To book it again and again, choose **Every day**, **Every weekday** or **Every week**, and the date it runs **until**. Each repeat is a booking of its own.

5. Press **Save**.

The booking is on the calendar; drag it to move it. A booking that overlaps another is refused, saying who has it and when, and if one repeat clashes, none is made. **Duplicate**, on an open booking, books the same instrument and times on another day.

Related: [Calendar](https://biomanager.org/guide/calendar) [Home](https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/book-equipment

---

## Sign a notebook page

When a page should be the record of your work, sign it: its text is fingerprinted and the page is locked.

Who and where: Whoever may edit the page · Desktop and lab server

1. Open the page in the Notebook.

2. Press **Sign** at the top of the page. The page's owner, and anyone it is shared with to edit, can sign it; anyone else can witness it once it is signed.

3. Under **What you are saying**, choose whether you did this work or reviewed the page.

4. Confirm who you are: **Your password**, or, if you sign in with Google or Microsoft, your user name.

5. Press **Sign and lock**.

Its exact text is fingerprinted and kept as a version, any live experiment in it is frozen as it is then, and the page is locked: nobody can change or delete it. The button now says **Signed**; it lists every signature, each showing whether the page still reads as it did when signed. A lab mate can open it and **Witness** the page.

> **Changing a signed page** Its owner presses **Signed**, writes **Why it is being amended** and presses **Open to amend**. The reason and every signature stay with the page; sign it again when it is done.

Related: [Signing a page](https://biomanager.org/guide/notebook#signing) [Notebook and utilities](https://biomanager.org/guide/notebook)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/sign-a-notebook-page

---

## Invite someone to the lab

Bring a new member onto your lab server: they make their own account, and an admin lets them in.

Who and where: Admins · Lab server

1. Send them your lab server's address.

2. They open it, press **Create an account** and fill it in. They can't sign in until an admin approves it. If the server offers it, they can also sign in with Google or Microsoft, or with the institution's own account, and connect it under **Settings → Sign-in methods**.

3. Admins are notified of the sign-up. Open **More → Manage users** at the foot of the sidebar.

4. Find the account marked *awaiting approval*, press **Approve**, and confirm.

5. For more than a member's rights, choose their role — *Member*, *Animal care*, *Facility manager* or *Admin* — and press **Set**.

They sign in with their own account and work as a member: they edit what they own and what is shared, and see the lab's databases. To share work with a few of them, put them in a [project group](https://biomanager.org/guide/project-groups).

> **Someone from outside the lab?** Give them a guest pass for a day to a month: **More → Guests**, who it's for and how long, **Make a code**. They open the link, enter the code, and work as a member with their own account until the pass ends or you press **End now**.

### Troubleshooting

#### They forgot their password

An admin resets it in **Manage users**.

Related: [People and guests](https://biomanager.org/guide/people-and-guests) [Who can do what](https://biomanager.org/guide/who-can-do-what) [Run it for your lab](https://biomanager.org/server)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/invite-someone

---

## Restore a backup

Put the desktop app's lab back as it was, from your own backup or from the copy BioManager kept before an update.

Who and where: Whoever uses that computer · Desktop app

1. Quit BioManager.

2. Open its data folder: `~/Library/Application Support/Biomanager/` on a Mac, `%APPDATA%\Biomanager\` on Windows, `~/.local/share/Biomanager/` on Linux. The lab's database is `data/biomanager.db`.

3. Move `data/biomanager.db` somewhere safe, rather than deleting it.

4. Put the backup in its place, named `biomanager.db`. From your Time Machine or File History copy of the folder; or one of the copies BioManager made before a new version changed the database, `data/backups/before-upgrade-….db` (the last ten are kept). Files added to records and pages are in the `uploads` folder; put it back from the same backup too.

5. Open BioManager. To undo an update, open it with the version you had before.

BioManager opens the lab as it was when that backup was made.

> **Newer changes aren't in a backup** Everything entered since the backup was made is not in it. Keep the file you moved aside until you are sure.

### On a lab server

A server backs up every night and restores the newest backup every week to prove it works. Restoring is one command, run by whoever looks after the server, and never deletes what it replaces: see `deploy/RUNBOOK.md` in the server bundle and [Keeping the data safe](https://biomanager.org/server#safe). For a mistake in a bulk change, **More → Batch history → Undo** is enough.

### Troubleshooting

#### BioManager won't start: the lab's database is an empty file

The file is 0 bytes, so its records are not in it. Put back a backup as above, or delete the empty file to start a new lab.

Related: [Your data and backups](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data) [Undo and history](https://biomanager.org/guide/undo-and-history) [Keeping the data safe](https://biomanager.org/server#safe)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/restore-a-backup

---

## Mouse colony

Mice, cages, litters and breeders, from birth to weaning: racks laid out like yours, and genotyping and weaning dates worked out for you.

Tabs across the top: **Mice**, **Cages**, **Litters**, **Breeders**, **Experiments**, **Strains** and **Dropdowns**. The **My colony / My groups / Shared / Everyone** switch changes what you *see*, never what you may edit: *My colony* is yours plus the shared cages you work in, *My groups* your [project groups'](https://biomanager.org/guide/project-groups), *Shared* just the shared cages, *Everyone* every cage. In the Cages tab, a chip for each purpose (*Experiments*, *Breeder*…) shows only those cages.

*The mouse sheet*

#### Racks and cages

**Cages → Rack grid → New rack**: rows, columns and how positions are labelled — `D7`, `4-7`, `7D` or 1 to 80, like the stickers on your real racks. Cages without a position wait in *Unplaced*; drag them on. Each cage has a purpose (breeding, stock, experiments), an owner, a room and its mice. Select cages to set purpose or owner, move them, or **Retire** them.

The cages show three ways. **Table**: one row per cage, each with its mice beneath it (edit them in place) and its actions; *Litter born* and *Wean due* come right after the mice, so when to wean is in view. Type over a cage's number to renumber it (its mice go with it; a number another cage has is refused). **Close all** folds every cage to its row (the page remembers), and **Open all** opens them again; the arrow at the start of a row or its mice count opens or closes one. **Cards**: a card for each cage — where it is, its purpose, owner, strain and when to wean, its mice and the same actions — with its own search and *Active, Breeding, Mine* filters. **Rack grid**: the racks from the front. The page remembers the one you used last.

*A rack grid*

#### Mice

- **New mouse** for one, **Add many** for a new group (or a CSV made from its **Download a template**), and **Import from Excel** for the sheet you already keep ([how](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in)). In Add many, type `new` as the cage to put a group in one new cage; with females and males, each sex gets its own new cage unless you tick *Keep both sexes in one new cage*. In the preview, `new-2`, `new-3`… are further new cages, and a new cage that would hold both sexes is pointed out.

- Each mouse has sex, date of birth (age shown in weeks), status — *breeder, experiment, geno, transfer, sac* — up to four transgenes, a genotype, cage, litter, owner and notes. A date of birth can't be in the future.

- Select mice to set a field (owner, status, transgenes, cage, note, date of death), **Add to experiment**, or **Sac**. Setting sac or a date of death ends the record; it stays in the history.

#### Breeding: from litter to weaning

On the **Cages** tab, open a breeding cage (its arrow or mice count) or find its card under **Cards**: **Litter born**, **Genotyping** and **Wean** are there, on cages whose purpose is *Breeder* or *Breeding*. **Create litter** numbers each litter L-1, L-2, L-3… (type your own ID instead if you like).

1. **Litter born** asks for the date of birth (today unless you change it; a date in the future is refused) and records the birth. BioManager works out weaning (P21) and genotyping (P28, or the day chosen in [Lab setup](https://biomanager.org/guide/lab-setup)), which appear on Home and the calendar when due — the same list in both. A cage holds one litter date, so a new litter replaces the last: if those pups are still in the cage, wean them first.

2. **Genotyping** asks for the father, mother and number of pups; **Create litter** makes the litter and a mouse for each pup, set to *geno*. They wait in the genotyping queue on Home until you change their **Status** from *geno*; entering a genotype alone doesn't take them off it.

3. **Wean** opens *Wean and distribute pups*, already filled with the cage's pups, females and males on separate rows: **Wean and move** sends each row to a new or existing cage, or **Mark weaned, move pups later**. Either way the litter is marked weaned and leaves Home and the calendar. Pups younger than P18 are weaned only after you confirm.

**Breeders** lists breeding cages — rack and position, how many of each sex — with their productivity, and flags breeders past 30 weeks. **Pick** takes a breeder as yours; its owner is notified.

#### Experiments, strains, dropdowns

- **Experiments** group mice into a cohort with treatment groups, what is done to them day by day and their body weights: see [Experiments, for every animal](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments). (The notebook's experiments are the write-ups; these are the animals.)

- **Strains** is the lab's reference list of lines and alleles.

- **Dropdowns** keeps the choices each column offers, so the lab uses the same words. Everyone sees them; only admins change them.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/mouse-colony

---

## Zebrafish

Tanks on racks, fish as groups or individuals, matings and clutches, lines with ZFIN names, and water quality.

- **Tanks**: **New tank** or **Add many** (consecutive IDs), on a table or a rack grid. Purposes: stock, breeding, mating, experiment, quarantine. Select tanks to set purpose or owner, move, or mark genotyping. The tank view also has the **Sacrifice log**.

- **Fish**: A group with a headcount, or individuals when you need them; statuses alive, transfer, geno, sac. Move or sac a selection.

- **Clutches**: **Set up a mating**: the male and female tanks, how many of each, and when they go back. Mating tanks due back show on Home until you mark them **Returned**. **New clutch** records each fertilisation.

- **Experiments**: Fish rows, a tank's fish or a clutch's larvae under a treatment, following their survival, length or a phenotype; **New experiment** can start with a tank's fish. See [Experiments](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments).

- **Lines**: Your line catalogue with ZFIN names and founders.

- **Water**: **Add system** for each recirculating system, and **Log reading** for temperature, pH, conductivity and salinity, with a chart. Tick **Raise an alarm with this reading** to flag a problem.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/zebrafish

---

## Flies and worms

Vials and plates on racks, with flips that follow the temperature.

Drosophila keeps **vials** in racks inside incubators; C. elegans keeps **plates** in boxes. Tabs: the vials or plates, **Schedule**, **Experiments**, **Genotypes**, **Incubators & racks**, **Frozen** (worms) and **Settings**.

1. Under **Incubators & racks**, add each incubator with its temperature, then racks or boxes inside it.

2. **New vial** (or plate): genotype, purpose and position. Fly purposes: stock, experiment, cross, virgins, progeny, expansion, backup. Worm purposes: maintenance, experiment, cross, progeny, synchronized, RNAi, males, starved.

3. **Schedule** shows what's overdue, today and coming up in the next 7, 14 or 30 days. Mark vials **Flipped** (worms: **Chunked**), **Collect eggs** into a new vial (worms: **Pick progeny**), and record scoring. Intervals follow the temperature: set them under **Settings → Temperatures and timing**, and a rack moved from 25 °C to 18 °C changes its schedule by itself.

4. In **Grid**, the line above a rack says when it was last flipped and when the next is due (red when overdue), and **Flipped today** beside Edit records a flip of the whole rack in one click (the rack list under **Incubators & racks** has the same button). Hover over the line for the rule it follows, e.g. *every 14 days at 25 °C*.

5. Worms: **New frozen lot** records a freeze; thaw one onto a new plate when you need it.

**Discard** retires a vial (it can be restored); **Copy to a new vial** starts the next generation. Settings also renames the words and purposes to your lab's.

*Fly vials*

*A fly rack as a grid, with its flip schedule above it*

The **Experiments** tab puts vials or plates under a drug, RNAi or a temperature shift and follows their survival; **New experiment** can start with a rack's vials. See [Experiments](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments).

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/flies-and-worms

---

## Any other organism

A database for any other organism, described in your own words.

**Add database** in the sidebar builds a database for anything else — Xenopus, axolotls, cell lines, yeast. Start from a mouse-like, zebrafish-like or blank organism and describe it:

- **Name and vocabulary** — what to call an animal, its housing (tank, cage, plate), a line, a birth cohort and a breeding event, and whether age is shown in days, weeks, days post-fertilisation, generations or passages (then Age shows the record's own *Passage* or *Generation* column, *P12*). The whole interface then speaks your words.

- **How animals are counted** — individuals, groups with a headcount, or groups with individuals when needed.

- **What it does** — tick what you need: housing and rack positions, lines, crosses and cohorts, pedigree, genotyping, schedules worked out from dates, environment readings, health, weights, a cull log, cryo stocks and more. Each has a one-line hint on the page. On the **Schedule**, **Done** takes the day it was really done; each rule counts from its own last Done, so feeding every two days doesn't restart a split due every four.

- **Your own columns** — text, long text, a genotype code, number, date, a choice, yes/no, a lab member, a link to a line, or a web link. They are edited in the sheet like the others, and **Set field** sets one on every ticked row.

- **Who it is for** — *Just me* (a personal database only you and admins see) or *The whole lab*.

Change any of it later under the database's **Configure**, without losing records. The same page offers inventories (samples, orders, reagents, antibodies, viruses, primers & oligos, cell lines, a custom list) and fly or worm stock databases. An icon is picked from a grid of the icons themselves; hover over one for its name.

*The Add database page*

Its **Experiments** tab works as the mouse colony's does, for your animals, groups and cohorts, and can start with a housing's animals: see [Experiments](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments).

### Troubleshooting

#### A colleague's database isn't in my sidebar

It may be their personal one (*Just you* on its tile), which only they and admins see, or an admin may have switched it off.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/any-organism

---

## Experiments, for every animal

Treatment groups, doses from body weight, readouts and the stats, for every animal.

Mice, zebrafish, flies, worms and your own organisms all have an **Experiments** tab beside their other tabs (Mice and Cages; Tanks and Fish; the vials or plates). **New experiment** there can start with a whole cage, tank, rack or housing of them. One page shows each experiment, and **All experiments** on it goes back to the tab.

| Mice | Mice, or a whole cage. Body weight (or tumour volume, a clinical score, survival). Injections, challenges, treatments, surgery, behaviour, sampling, imaging. |
|---|---|
| Zebrafish | Fish rows, a whole tank, or a clutch's larvae. Survival (how many of those at the start are alive), standard length or a phenotype. Drug in the water, microinjection, heat shock, injury or fin clip. |
| Flies and worms | Vials or plates, or a whole rack; say how many each started with. They have no body weight: survival, or eclosion and climbing for flies, brood size and paralysis for worms. Drug in the food or on the plate, RNAi feeding, temperature shifts, starvation, infection, flipping to fresh food. |
| Any other organism | Animals, groups or cohorts, or a whole housing. Body weight, length, survival or a score. |

Any experiment can follow a readout of its own (**Readout → Something else…**): a number for each, or how many of those at the start.

#### The page

- **The experiment** on top: name, status, start (day 1), end, readout and description, saved as you type.

- **The sheet of its animals** switches between **Treatment** — each manipulation day a column: ✓ and the amount for each animal that got it (click to change) — and the readout, a column a day, typed in place (**Another day** adds one). Each animal's group is edited here too.

- **Record manipulation** records what was just done — *the HDM group got Tamoxifen 20 mg/kg i.p. today* — or a day of the regimen. For a dose per body weight it works out each animal's amount from its latest weight, and the volume given the solution (*10 mg/mL*). Tick the animals it was done to, pick the **Reagent used** (its lot is kept; an expired one is flagged) and, if you want, **make a sample record for each one** in Samples, with the animal as its source.

- **The chart** shows the readout by group over the days (the value, or its % of the first; for a count, % of those at the start). Each manipulation day is a dashed line: point at it to see what was done that day, by whom. Stars mark the days the groups differ, and **Tests by day** below lists each test (Welch's t-test for two groups, one-way ANOVA for more, χ² for counts), each day on its own.

#### The regimen

**Regimen** lists what is to be done and on which days: the kind, what, dose, route, solution, group and days (`1`, `2-5`, `2/3/4/5`, `1, 8, 15`). Day 1 is the start date. The days to do are on the calendar, and the experiment's owner gets a notification each morning of what is due (turn it off in **Settings → Notifications → Experiments**). Nothing is done until someone records it on the page. **Save as a regimen…** keeps it to plan the next cohort from.

#### At the bench, and afterwards

- **Bench mode** (scan its QR code with a phone): pick what you are doing, then one animal at a time with big numbers — type each weight or count, or give each today's manipulation and tap **Given ✓**; record it at the end. **Scan a card** reads a cage, tank or vial card with the phone's camera and jumps to the animal in it.

- **Export** downloads an Excel workbook: the readout, long (for Prism or R) and wide, each animal's manipulations, and the tests by day.

- **Add to notebook** makes your notebook page for the experiment, with a live view of its manipulations and readout (`/experiment` adds one to any page; **Freeze a copy** keeps it as it is now).

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments

---

## Plasmids

Plasmid records with their sequence and map, and the box each tube is in.

- At the top, tabs for the databases that go with plasmids — **Primers**, **Glycerol stocks**, **Viruses** — in the order the work runs. Each is an ordinary database with its own sheet ([see them](https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders)); they share one place in the sidebar because each names the plasmid it came from.

- Show them as a **Table**, by storage **Boxes**, or as a **List**; chips for *Mine*, *Has sequence*, *In a box*.

- **Sequence**, beside each plasmid's number in the table, opens its sequence and map (**Add sequence** when it has none yet); the number opens the same page.

- **New plasmid** takes a name, backbone, insert, resistance, owner and a box position (blank takes the next free one) — or paste a list of names to make several. Drop in a SnapGene `.dna`, GenBank, FASTA or plain-text sequence: its name, features and every annotation note come with it, and a file of several sequences keeps the first and says so.

- Open a plasmid to see its sequence and features on an interactive map you can edit (edits save themselves), full screen if you like. **Download** above the map gives it as GenBank (with every feature) or FASTA. **Versions**, below the map, lists every earlier sequence (replaced, cleared or edited) with **Restore**. **Storage** and **Properties** are the other tabs. On **Properties**, **Made from** records its backbone, insert or template (a plasmid in the lab, by number or name, or one from outside it such as *Addgene #11150*) and how it was made; the page then shows **Made from** and **Used to make** above the map, and a **Family tree** both ways. **Storage** also lists its [glycerol stocks](https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders), with the box each is in, and the viruses made from it ([Viruses](https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders)). Its address carries its number: plasmid #12 is `…/plasmid/12`.

- The **Feature library** (a link at the top of Plasmids) keeps the lab's elements by sequence: promoters, ITRs and LTRs, WPRE, resistance genes, tags. **Add to library**, above a well-annotated map (a SnapGene or Addgene file, say), keeps its named features there; an admin can **Collect from every plasmid**. On the library page, **Read elements from files** takes them straight from annotated files — the GenBank a repository gives you, a SnapGene `.dna`, a vendor's map — several at once, without making a plasmid for each. Nothing is built in: every element is one your own files carry, because a sequence typed from memory and wrong by one base would mislabel every map in the lab. An admin can also fetch the **common-features pack** — about 1,900 elements curated from some 2,000 widely used plasmids, downloaded from the open research archive when you ask for it (about a minute; the page shows it when it is in). Its authors built it by exporting a commercial program's published library, so check anything you rely on; elements you added yourself always win over it. Search the library by name or by sequence. On any other plasmid, **Detect features** marks each library element wherever it is, on either strand and across the origin, and keeps the map as it was in **Versions**.

- **Assemble a plasmid**, from the top of Plasmids or from above any map, builds the next plasmid out of the ones you have. Fill the tray with fragments — a whole plasmid, one of its features, a region between two bases, or a piece an enzyme leaves — in the order they go together, turning any of them round, and put them together three ways: **digest and ligate** (cut with the same enzymes and let the sticky ends meet), **Gibson / NEBuilder HiFi** (neighbouring fragments share twenty-odd bases where they meet; the wizard designs the primers that add them, each with its melting temperature) or **Golden Gate** (BsaI, BsmBI or BbsI, which cut outside their own site, so every junction is a four-base overhang you chose). When you cut a plasmid, only the enzymes that actually have a site in it are offered, with how many sites each has and the single cutters first, and the piece you pick is drawn on a ring of the plasmid it came off, so you can see which part comes out before you take it. Each junction shows its own bases, and one line tells you what is wrong and which end it is — *Fragment 2's 3′ end has no overlap with fragment 3* — rather than that it did not work. A Golden Gate is refused when two junctions take the same overhang, when one is another backwards, or when one reads the same on both strands, because each of those puts the pieces together in more than one way. You see the product's map, its length and every fragment in it before anything is made. **Create the plasmid** then makes an ordinary plasmid: the features of each fragment at their new places (a feature a cut runs through keeps the part that is there, and says so), each fragment marked on the map so you can see the joins, **Made from** filled in for every plasmid it came out of with the enzymes and coordinates used, the first entry in its **Versions**, and the library's elements marked if you asked. A Gibson's primers are saved in the [Primers](https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders) database marked *to order* and drawn on the map of the plasmid each one amplifies, so **Copy for ordering** picks them up with the rest.

- If your lab runs a server, whoever looks after it can install **pLannotate** (a separate, free program) and **Annotate with pLannotate** then appears above the map. It finds elements by comparing sequences rather than matching them exactly, so it catches a codon-optimised gene or a promoter a base or two off, which the library on its own will miss. Everything it marks is kept in **Versions**, so it can be undone.

- **Files**, on **Storage**, keeps what belongs with the plasmid: the sequencing reads (.ab1) that confirmed it, gel photos, the vendor's datasheet. Say in one line what they show. Pictures show a thumbnail; whoever added a file, or an admin, can take it off again. They come with your data in **Export my data**.

- A primer you draw on the map (select bases, then **Edit → Create → Primer**) is also kept in the lab's [Primers](https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders) database, marked *to order*, with the plasmid in its **Plasmid** column. The **Primers** card under the map lists every primer for this plasmid, where it binds and any 5′ tail; tick some, then **Copy for ordering** (name and sequence, one per line, to paste into a supplier's form) or **Export for ordering** (a CSV).

- Each tube keeps its miniprep's **Concentration** (ng/µL) and **260/280**, in the sheet and on its **Storage** tab, which also lists the notebook pages that link it.

- **Belongs to**: *Personal*, or *Lab common* — anyone can edit it (a shared stock plasmid), while only its owner or an admin changes whose it is or deletes it. The *Lab common* chip lists them.

- Select plasmids to set owner, resistance or Belongs to, move them to a box, or delete. Moved into another box with no position, a plasmid takes its next free cell. **Import from Excel** brings in your old list.

*A plasmid map*

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/plasmids

---

## Samples, orders, reagents, antibodies, viruses

Samples, orders, reagents, antibodies, viruses, primers, glycerol stocks and cell lines.

One engine, nine starting points, each with its own columns and statuses. Viruses, Primers and Glycerol stocks each name the plasmid they came from, so they sit with [Plasmids](https://biomanager.org/guide/plasmids) as tabs of one area rather than on their own in the sidebar:

| Samples | Tissue and material, linked to the animal it came from — pick the colony and type its ID in the **Source** cell, or tick a whole harvest and set it on all of them at once — stored at RT, 4 °C, −20 °C, −80 °C or LN₂ in a freezer box position, with what was measured as numbers: *Conc.* and its unit, *260/280*, *260/230*, *Volume (µL)*. Available, in use, used up, discarded. |
|---|---|
| Orders | What the lab has asked for: vendor, catalogue number, quantity, price, grant account. Requested, ordered, received, cancelled — on a table or a **Board** you drag cards across. |
| Reagents | Quantity, concentration, CAS number, storage temperature, hazard, lot and expiry. In stock, low, empty, discarded. |
| Antibodies | Host, clonality, clone, conjugate, reactivity, applications, dilution, isotype, RRID, and where each vial is. |
| Viruses | AAV, lentivirus, rabies and other vectors: serotype, the plasmid it was made from (**Made from**), promoter, payload, titer, biosafety level, the date made, and each aliquot's place in a −80 °C box. The DNA icon beside the plasmid opens its sequence and map to read (editing stays on the plasmid's own page). In stock, low, used up, discarded. |
| Primers & oligos | Sequence (5′→3′), direction, target, its pair, stock µM and modification. *Length*, *GC %* and *Tm* are worked out from the sequence (nearest neighbour, 50 mM Na⁺, 250 nM). **Add primer pair** makes *name*-F and *name*-R at once, each naming the other, side by side in a box. A primer drawn on a plasmid's map comes here by itself, with the plasmid in its **Plasmid** column. Tick primers, then **Copy for ordering** or **Export for ordering** for the supplier. To order, ordered, in stock, low, used up, discarded. |
| Glycerol stocks | Bacteria carrying a plasmid, frozen in glycerol: the plasmid (**Plasmid**), strain, colony, resistance, how it was checked (digest, colony PCR, Sanger, whole plasmid), the date frozen, and its place in a −80 °C box. The plasmid's **Storage** tab lists its glycerol stocks and the box each is in. In stock, low, used up, discarded. |
| Cell lines | A frozen vial of each line or clone: species, parent, passage, freeze date, cells per vial, medium, selection, mycoplasma result and date, and its place in the LN₂ boxes. In stock, thawed, used up, discarded. |
| Custom list | Whatever you define. |

#### Ordering, start to shelf

1. **New order.** Item, vendor, catalogue number and quantity are required (starred), so no order goes out half-filled. Type an item or catalogue number the lab has used before and pick it: the vendor, price and grant fill in from last time. The lab's admins are told of each new request.

2. **Follow it.** The status chips — *Requested, Ordered, Received, Cancelled* — show each stage in one tap; the person who requested it is notified as it moves.

3. **It arrives.** Mark it received and BioManager asks **Add it to stock?**: a new reagent, antibody or virus with its name, vendor, catalogue number, lot, quantity and expiry already filled in, opened for you to add where it's kept. (Later, the **To stock** button on the order does the same.) From then on the order shows *Reagents #8* and the reagent shows the order it came from; each opens the other.

4. **Running low?** On any reagent, antibody or virus, the cart button, **Order again**, opens a new order with its details and the quantity, price and grant of the last time it was ordered. While it is already on order the button says **On order**, and the new order opens with a note naming the open one and who asked for it.

#### Every inventory

- **Mine** and **Lab common** keep your own stock apart from the lab's shared shelf.

- *Expiring soon* (30 days) and *Expired* chips; expired and low stock also show on Home.

- **Box grid** places items in freezer boxes; the same boxes as everywhere else. A box's *Stored at* (−80 °C, LN₂…) goes to what is put in it, and moving the box moves theirs. In a box with no position given, an item takes the next free one. Marking a tube used up, empty or discarded frees its position; its location note keeps where it was. **New box** has **How many**, for a whole tower at once.

- **Used in notebook pages**, at the bottom of a record's dialog, lists the pages that link it (`@antibodies 5`; see [Notebook](https://biomanager.org/guide/notebook)).

- **Configure** (its creator, or an admin): the name, what it tracks, the choices and statuses (renaming one relabels its items), your own columns, and which fields are **needed for a new item**.

- **A plasmid column** (the Viruses' **Made from**, or one you add in Configure as *A plasmid*): type the plasmid's number or name, or pick it from the list, and the cell opens that plasmid. The plasmid's **Storage** tab lists everything made from it, under *Made from this plasmid*.

*The reagents sheet*

*The orders board*

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders

---

## Calendar

Experiments, to-dos and bookings, with the colony's dates filled in for you.

- **Month, Week, Day** and **List** views. Filled in for you: weanings, genotyping and sac reminders, fly and worm flips and egg collections, organism schedules, zebrafish tanks and reagent expiry. Clicking one (once, in every view) opens the record it came from. A link can open a given view and day: `/calendar?view=week&date=2026-10-05`.

- The sidebar has a small month to jump around, a **Show** list with a colour and a count for each kind (events, to-dos, the colony, stocks and organisms, supplies, protocols, equipment, time away, connected calendars), the instruments and the protocols under way.

- **New event** offers an event, a to-do (due today, tomorrow, next week, or a date), **Book equipment**, **Time away** and **Start a protocol**. Drag an event, to-do or booking to move it.

- **Who sees it**, for an event or a to-do: *Only me*, *Everyone in the lab* or one of your [project groups](https://biomanager.org/guide/project-groups). Your own is seen by nobody else, admins included. A shared event is changed only by whoever added it and admins; a shared to-do anyone it is for can tick off. A new event starts as the lab's, a new to-do as yours.

- **Repeats**: an event every N days, weeks or months, or every month on the same weekday (*the first Monday*), until a date. **Delete this one** takes out a single date and **Change this one only** moves or changes it alone; Save changes every repeat.

- **Protocols**: write the steps once in days from day 0 (tamoxifen days 0–4, implant day 14, perfuse day 42), then start it for an experiment or a cohort. Every step lands on its day; move day 0 and they all move. A run keeps the steps it started with if the protocol is edited later. (These put the days on the calendar; the notebook's protocols hold the bench steps.)

- **Equipment**: add the lab's instruments under **Manage**, and **Edit** one there to rename it, say where it is or change its colour; its bookings follow. A booking that overlaps another is refused, saying who has it and when. A new booking can repeat every day, weekday or week until a date — each repeat is a booking of its own, and if one clashes none is made. **Duplicate**, on an open booking, books the same instrument and times on another day.

- **Time away**: leave or a conference. **Away soon** lists what of theirs falls due meanwhile — animals, vials, to-dos, bookings, protocol steps — and asks who covers it; that person is told.

- **Connected calendars** shows Google Calendar and any iCal subscription alongside, read-only.

- **On your phone**: a private link (just your things, or the whole lab's) for Apple, Google or Outlook Calendar. It updates about every hour. **Make a new link** stops the old one working.

*The calendar*

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/calendar

---

## Notebook and utilities

Notebook pages, protocols, data sheets, signing, and the bench calculators.

#### Pages

- Pages in **Topics**, written like a document and kept as Markdown. A new page goes in the topic you have open, or in *Inbox* when none is (experiments and meetings go to their own topics). Type **/** at the start of a line for a menu of blocks: tables, plots, protocols, calculators and the rest below. **Templates**: ⋯ → **Save as template**, and start new pages from it (a name you already use asks before replacing that template). It keeps the page's type (an Experiment template makes Experiments); **Structure only** keeps the headings, steps and table headers and leaves out the results, ticks, readings, pictures and what was written under Results, Observations or Conclusion; **Share it with the lab** offers it to everyone.

- Type `@` to link a mouse, plasmid, order or any inventory record — an antibody, a sample, a primer (`@antibodies 5`), found by its name, catalogue number or lot (a lot or catalogue number typed in full, like `@0012`, comes first; names such as *anti-β-actin* or *Waf1/Cip1* are found as written), a database by its name (`@antib` offers *Antibodies*, and picking it lists its records), or a colleague (`@jordan`, for action items); the page and the record then point at each other, and the record lists the page under **Used in notebook pages**. The chip shows the record's name after its number (*@antibodies 5 · anti-p53*). Hover over one for its details; clicking it opens the record, and **↗** (or `⌘`/`Ctrl`-click) opens it in a new BioManager tab.

- **Daily log** (*Today*) and **Meetings**: a presenter rotation, shared meeting notes, and action items (`- [ ] @name …, due …`) sent to that person's to-dos — from any page, with ⋯ → **Send @name tasks as to-dos**.

- An AI assistant you connected can add lines to the **Log** of today's daily log, once you approve them ([AI assistants](https://biomanager.org/guide/ai-assistants)). If the page is open, the line appears in it within a few seconds.

#### Experiments and protocols

- **Experiments**: aim, setup, samples and lot numbers, steps, results. *Start* and *Finished* stamp the times; planned, running, done or failed shows in the sidebar. (The colony's **Experiments** tab groups the animals.)

- **Colony experiment** (`/experiment`) shows an experiment on any of your animals in the page: each day's manipulation, when it was done and by whom, the amount each mouse got, and the body weights as a table and a chart (grams or % of the first weight, with the manipulation days marked). It stays up to date; **Freeze a copy** keeps what it shows now in the page, so later changes to the experiment don't alter your record. On the experiment itself, **Add to notebook** makes your page for it with this block already in.

- **Protocols** with numbered versions. *Start an experiment from it* copies the steps as a checklist and records the version; **Run mode** takes you through it at the bench, one step at a time. **Protocols** in the sidebar (or `/protocol`) opens the library: the lab's protocols and a dozen common ones built in, to insert or copy.

#### Data and calculators

- **Data sheets**: paste from Excel or a CSV, add formula columns, and get a plot (bar, dot, box, scatter, line) with error bars, a fitted line and a t-test, Mann–Whitney or ANOVA. **Plate reader** and **qPCR** blocks read concentrations off a standard curve and ΔΔCt fold changes.

- **Buffer recipes** scale with the volume; common buffers are built in and the lab's own are shared. **Calculators** for dilution, molarity, master mix, serial dilution, ligation, cells, gels, DNA/RNA and **Protein (A₂₈₀)**: paste the sequence (or give ε and MW) and the reading, and it gives µM and mg/mL. Durations in a step get a **⏱** timer, named from the step's own words; time points (*6, 24, 48 h*, *at 24 h*, *the 48 h samples*) don't. Times on a page (*started 16:00*) are on the lab's clock, whatever your computer's time zone.

#### Signing a page

When a page should be the record of your work, **Sign** it — your choice, page by page; nothing asks you to. You confirm who you are (your password, or your user name if you sign in with Google or Microsoft) and what signing means. Its exact text is fingerprinted and kept as a version, any live experiment in it is frozen as it is then, and the page is locked: nobody can change or delete it. A lab mate can **Witness** it. To change it, its owner **Amends** it with a reason; the reason and every signature stay with the page, each showing whether the page still reads as it did when signed.

#### Working together

Share a page to read or edit, with people, everyone in the lab or a [project group](https://biomanager.org/guide/project-groups); editors type in it at the same time. Comments on a passage, with `@name` telling that person (switch these notices off under **Settings → Notifications**). **Version history** keeps every editing session to compare or restore. **Tags and search** work across every page you can open.

#### Utilities

**Utilities**, under Notebook in the sidebar, holds 41 bench calculators. Find one in the list or type in **Find a calculator** (plain letters do: *a260*, *ddct*, or what you are doing, like *nanodrop*); the answer changes as you type, each remembers what you last typed in it on this computer, and **Reset** goes back to its example. Most solve for whichever field you leave empty (it is marked), and units are yours to choose.

- **Solutions & buffers**: Molarity; dilution (C₁V₁ = C₂V₂); serial dilutions; percent solutions; ×-fold stocks; mass ↔ molar concentration; buffer pH (Henderson–Hasselbalch, with the temperature); osmolarity; another form of a chemical (a hydrate or salt for the one in the recipe). Type a chemical's name or formula to fill its molecular weight, from the lab's own list first (*MgCl2·6H2O* and *magnesium chloride hexahydrate* are the same one); one it doesn't know leaves the weight for you to type.

- **DNA & RNA**: Concentration from A₂₆₀; mass ↔ moles ↔ copies; oligo Tm, GC, MW and resuspension volume; ligation insert:vector; HiFi/Gibson assembly; PCR and qPCR master mixes; qPCR efficiency from a standard curve; ΔΔCt fold change; transformation efficiency.

- **Protein**: Concentration from A₂₈₀; MW, ε and pI from the sequence; a standard curve (BCA, Bradford, ELISA) read off for your samples; SDS-PAGE gel recipes; µg per lane.

- **Cells**: Haemocytometer counts; seeding plates (by vessel); doubling time; scaling a transfection; virus for an MOI; lentivirus titer from % positive cells; freezing down; drug and vehicle for treatments.

- **Bacteria & yeast**: OD₆₀₀ to cells and dilutions; time to reach an OD; antibiotic for plates and media.

- **Centrifuge, animals & gels**: rpm ↔ × g; dose by body weight; agarose gels; radioactive decay.

- **Numbers & units**: Mean, SD, SEM and CV; animals or samples per group; a unit converter.

**Reference tables**, below the calculator: culture vessels, buffers, antibiotics, agarose gels, isotopes and molecular weights. A link to a calculator (`…/utilities#dilution`) opens it.

*Utilities*

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/notebook

---

## Who can do what

Who can see and change what in a lab: members, owners and admins.

- **You edit what you own** — your mice, cages, vials, plasmids and items.

- **Shared cages and anything marked lab common** belong to the whole lab.
